findings.title: Detach asynchronous writes from request cancellation
findings.body: The legacy-write timeout is derived from the incoming request context, which is canceled when the HTTP handler returns. Since Create now returns without waiting for the goroutine, the legacy operation can receive an already-canceled context or be canceled midway through its write, regardless of the ten-second timeout. The same issue affects Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection. Preserve context values but detach request cancellation before applying the background-write timeout.

findings.title: Replicate the committed update rather than reapplying UpdatedObjectInfo
findings.body: Legacy.Update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the wrapper containing the object committed to unified storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute a patch or server-side apply against the old object supplied by each store; if legacy is behind, reapplying it there can produce a different object or fail despite a successful unified update. The previous implementation explicitly passed the unified result to legacy. Replicate a snapshot of res rather than evaluating the original update against legacy state again.

findings.title: Preserve operation ordering for background replication
findings.body: Each successful mutation launches an independent goroutine with no ordering between writes to the same resource. For example, a client can create a resource and then delete it after Create returns, while the legacy delete executes before the legacy create; the delete fails with not-found and the later create leaves a deleted resource in legacy permanently. Successive updates can likewise overwrite newer legacy data with older data. Serialize or queue replication per resource so the legacy safety copy follows committed operation order.

findings.title: Correct storage metric attribution and resource labels
findings.body: The successful Delete metric uses the object name as the kind label, creating a separate metric series for every deleted resource rather than the bounded kind label. Other new metric calls also attribute operations to the wrong backend: failed unified Create and Update call recordLegacyDuration (lines 45 and 129), while background legacy DeleteCollection calls recordStorageDuration (line 166). These errors both risk unbounded metric cardinality on deletes and make backend error rates and latency measurements incorrect.
